niche: a New Zealand District Court region's first appearances from police custody, where the gap in remands in custody between defendants without their own lawyer and defendants with one widened in the twelve months to 30 September 2026: where in the region's custody lists the widening sits and which initiative on the region's Budget 2027 shortlist removes it (electronically monitored bail assessment capacity, a judge on the custody list, the duty lawyer roster, supported bail accommodation, court-date text reminders)
answer: Duty lawyer roster: a second rostered duty lawyer at Kestrel Bay District Court on every sitting day
analyst_test: A strong analyst who measures the first-appearance custody-remand gap by counsel status within each court and judicial officer, with the legally relevant pre-decision factors (charge seriousness, criminal history, bail history, on bail at arrest) as controls, finds the widening in the Kestrel Bay custody list under the community magistrate who took it over in March 2026 and funds a judge on the custody list; read against the duty lawyer service's own record and the court's sitting calendar, most of those matters were called while the single rostered duty lawyer was serving the new audio-visual remand list in the next courtroom, the gap is the same under every judicial officer once those matters are set apart, and only the duty lawyer roster removes it.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the disparity in remands in custody between defendants with and without their own counsel at first appearance, estimated within court and judicial officer net of the legally relevant pre-decision factors the way bail disparity analysis estimates it, where the decisive judgment is what the within-officer comparison compares when one officer's sitting hours coincide with the duty lawyer's absence; with a hospital's or a lender's nouns there is no bail decision, no legally relevant factor set and no duty lawyer standing between a defendant and a remand, so the task stops making sense.

driver: The decisive quantity is whether the advocate who stands between an unrepresented case and the decision was in the room when the case was called, read off the advocate's own service record against a second list the same advocate was rostered to serve next door: the advocate's daily presence and volume are flat, the decision-maker who took over the overlapping hours carries the whole widening on a within-decision-maker comparison, and only setting apart the cases called while the advocate was in the other room shows the gap is the same under every decision-maker and belongs to the roster.
driver_concrete: From March 2026 Kestrel Bay District Court sat a new audio-visual remand list in courtroom 2 on mornings that overlap the custody list in courtroom 1, and the region's duty lawyer roster kept one duty lawyer there; custody-list defendants called while the duty lawyer was on the audio-visual list stood unassisted and were remanded in custody far more often, the community magistrate who took over the custody list that March presides over most of those hours, and only the duty lawyer service's time-stamped record, set against each matter's call time, shows the widening is the roster's and not the bench's or electronically monitored bail's.
stump: A competent solver measures the first-appearance custody-remand gap within court and judicial officer with the legally relevant factors as controls, finds the widening in the Kestrel Bay custody list under the community magistrate who took it over in March 2026, and funds a judge on the custody list; the step that lands it there is reading a within-officer difference as the officer's, when the duty lawyer service's record and the sitting calendar show the single rostered duty lawyer was serving the new audio-visual remand list next door when most of the widening's matters were called, which puts the gap on the duty lawyer roster.

differentiation.task274: task274 (a county's pre-plea diversion lottery read at a cut while most offered cases are still inside the programme) spends a deferred outcome and a cumulative incidence completed through a termination hazard; task399 has no lottery, no programme stage and no pending outcome: every first appearance is decided on the day, and the step is which matters were called while the duty lawyer was serving another list.
differentiation.task121: task121 v6 rebuilds the rest each worker actually had from the operator's own event record against the schedule; task399 reads no schedule against an actual: the sitting calendar is accurate, and the step is the overlap between one advocate's two lists, set against each matter's call time, behind a within-officer disparity.
differentiation.task111: task111 finds which cause still operates in the forward window when overflow work lands on the primary workforce late in the day; task399 sizes nothing forward and has no overflow: the decisive record is one advocate's presence at each matter's call across two simultaneous lists.
differentiation.task399: architecture 3 rebuilt a slot stock from releases, bookings and returns behind a booking journey and died on the throughput identity; architecture 4 rebuilds no stock and has no throughput: the advocate's output is flat by construction and the decisive relation is presence at the call.
differentiation.task253: task253 v2 values the loss of one of several parallel links sharing a congestible capacity by re-solving the self-consistent loading with the link removed; task399 loads nothing and solves no fixed point: the shared limit is one advocate rostered to two simultaneous lists, and the decisive record is whether the advocate was in the room at each matter's call.
differentiation.task141: task141 v1 prices a let-everyone-through rule from the outcome gradient across decision-makers who sit by rota and let through different shares; task399 prices no rule and reads no gradient across officers: the within-officer gap it finds is the advocate's absence at the call, and the gap is the same under every officer once those calls are set apart.
differentiation.task461: surface pair (0.101, corpus top 1 per cent): task461 conforms a battery node spread series to a hub record for a cycling threshold (ETL); task399 shares only the pdf and xlsx deliverable pair, nothing of world, data or insight
differentiation.task131: surface pair (0.101, corpus top 1 per cent): task131 reads a randomised tariff trial for a default design (causal); task399 shares only the pdf and xlsx deliverable pair, nothing of world, data or insight

lineage.architecture: v1 (Quantitative Finance: a manufacturer's pension plan's global equity programme, which of five initiatives to fund against the shortfall to its policy benchmark)
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the money a parent raised for its own payments and left waiting in one unit's account, recorded there as the unit's holding: a unit-level attribution books its cost to the unit as a low market exposure and credits the candidate that would keep that money invested with almost nothing, while the money's own path puts it with the parent and makes that candidate the largest.
lineage.fate: spent at the draw on 2026-11-03: it collided with task398's draw in the same cell (quantitative-finance / factor-return-attribution / root-cause), registered earlier but not visible to this guard; guard.py check with task398 visible returned BLOCK ban.pairing, ban.subdomain, ban.artifact (filed_standard) and ban.strategy (decomposition_attribution), and a reviewer would read the two as the same decision (an equity programme's shortfall against its benchmark and which of five changes removes most of it)

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the rest a worker actually got, rebuilt from the operation's own event record rather than from the schedule: running late, the operation works straight through the scheduled rests, so a schedule-based fatigue analysis puts the rising risk on long shifts and the candidate that would restore the rests looks worth nothing, while measured on the rest actually taken the long-shift effect vanishes and that candidate is the largest.
lineage.architecture: v2 (Human Factors: a regional bus operator, drivers safety events against the terminus stands the schedule promised)
lineage.fate: spent at the draw on 2026-11-03: same cell and same decisive insight as shipped task121 v6 (rest rebuilt from the operator records), a template the lexical guard misses (driver score 0.06); nine axes equal to task121 (domain, subdomain, objective, shape 18, gate_g, strategy, decision type, question form what, org family)

lineage.architecture: v3 (Product Analytics: Norland Driver Services, a provincial licensing agency's road-test booking journey, which of five 2027 initiatives removes the fall in new drivers licensed)
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the stock of a capacity that sits behind a self-service journey, rebuilt day by day from its own releases, bookings and returns: where the stock is empty the journey's searches fail without any record of the shortage, so a stage-by-stage reading puts the fall on the step where users gave up and on the release that changed that step, while read against the stock open at each search the step is sound and the candidate that adds capacity is the largest.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 2 on 2026-11-03 before any data was cut: the pricing harness (scratch a3/harness.py, a daily road-test booking queue over two years) measured two one-group-by routes to the golden in all three hiding variants (the busy centres losing 14 per cent of slots; the province's releases held flat by rural top-ups; a quarter of slots released four days ahead): releases by centre fell about 8 per cent at the busy centres and bookings over releases by centre sat at the ceiling there, so the throughput identity (tests sat at a fully booked centre equal its releases) makes the capacity fall one subtraction (readability tests 3 and 6, Gate F's two cheap routes)
